runs.text: Our project aims to engineer BtSULT to catalyze the sulfonation of lithocholic acid (LCA), potentially improving bile acid metabolism in individuals experiencing debilitating post-cholecystectomy syndrome (PCS). The goal of our in vitro trials was to express, quantify, purify, and evaluate the structural and functional properties of our target sulfotransferase enzyme.

runs.text: Laboratory experimentation is an essential pillar in synthetic biology for testing the real-world behavior of designed biological parts and systems. Our wet lab workflow primarily involves completing robust assays to quantify LCA sulfation activity of the reengineered BtSULT enzyme.

Bacterial Transformation and Host Expression
Transforming BL21 Cells

runs.text: BL21 E. coli cells acted as the host for re-engineered BtSULT transformation. We elected the pET_28a(+) backbone as a vector to hold our gene insert for convenience of the T7 promoter region. This promoter region is highly transcribed by abundant T7 RNA polymerase in BL21 cells, focusing the cells' resources on creating an abundance of recombinant protein. We also used the selective antibiotic
to limit streaked bacterial cultures and other contaminants from growing without the included resistance gene (Kan. R).

runs.text: Bacterial transformation is a process in which foreign DNA is introduced into bacterial cells, leading to new genetic traits being expressed by the bacteria host. By having E-coli BL21 bacterial cells uptake plasmid DNA, we were able to produce our desired protein.

Colony PCR

runs.text: Grown cultures were then further screened for containing gene inserts by Colony PCR. Primers for the T7 promoter were used to identify the presence of the gene. Colonies were evaluated using band size relative to a 1kB ladder, since primers that sit in the vector backbone produce a baseline-sized DNA band if the gene insert is missing, and a larger band that includes the insert if cloning succeeded.

Bacterial Growth and Induction
Growth Conditions and IPTG/Allolactase

runs.text: Gene-positive cultures of streaked bacteria were inoculated overnight at 350 rpm and 37°C, reaching an OD600 of 1.0 (cultures that overgrew were diluted to reach the density). These inoculations were spiked into larger liquid cultures at a ratio of 1:100 (v/v) and shaken at 150-200 rpm and 37°C, till cultures reached an OD600 of 0.4–0.8, indicating logarithmic phases of growth (usually within 2- 4 hours). At this phase, 0.7 mM isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) or 1% nonfat dry milk powder (cost-effective and resourceful allolactase supplement for insufficient IPTG) was added to disburden the lacI repressor and shift cell metabolism from growth to protein

Cell Lysis and His-Tag Purification

runs.text: Cell lysis was performed on pelleted and thawed bacterial cells using non-ionic 20 mM Tris•HCl buffer at pH 7.5 (B-PER™ Bacterial Protein Extraction Reagent from Thermo Fisher #90084), including lysozyme, protease inhibitor tablets, and DNase. Lysed bacteria were then purified using Nickel-charged His-Affinity Gel [IMAC] (His-Spin Protein Miniprep Zymo Cat #P2002) and eluted using supplied elution buffer (8M urea, 250 mM imidazole, 0.1 M sodium phosphate monobasic, 0.01 M Tris, pH 4.5).

Bicinchoninic Acid Assay Quantification

runs.text: Eluted protein and crude lysate samples were both quantified using BCA Quantification in a 96-well plate and read at 595 nm. Dilution curve wells were made with Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA), with 8 dilution-standardized samples ranging from 2000ug/mL to 15.625ug/mL of BSA. Standard wells were made in the buffers for each sample: elution buffer and lysis buffer, respectively. A working reagent containing Cu
ions is added to the samples, so that peptide bonds in the protein undergo chelation and form Cu
in the alkaline environment. These ions react with bicinchoninic acid (BCA) to form a purple-colored complex that absorbs light around 562 nm and provides a means of quantification.

blocks.text: Eluted protein and crude lysate samples were both quantified using BCA Quantification in a 96-well plate and read at 595 nm. Dilution curve wells were made with Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA), with 8 dilution-standardized samples ranging from 2000ug/mL to 15.625ug/mL of BSA. Standard wells were made in the buffers for each sample: elution buffer and lysis buffer, respectively. A working reagent containing Cu2+ ions is added to the samples, so that peptide bonds in the protein undergo chelation and form Cu+ in the alkaline environment. These ions react with bicinchoninic acid (BCA) to form a purple-colored complex that absorbs light around 562 nm and provides a means of quantification.

blocks.text: Discussion

Over two cycles, we built a working expression-and-analysis pipeline for BtSULT variants in BL21 cells: heat-shock transformation, kanamycin selection, colony PCR, induction, B-PER lysis, His-tag purification, and BCA quantification. Cycle 3 with WT and the 6xAla SulFlux showed that both constructs integrate and express. Several colonies carried the expected 2 kb band, and His-purified proteins reached 54–102 µg/mL, about 21–38% of the loaded sample. Cycle 4 (F147S, F147S_E144D, and WT) reproduced this at higher yields, with roughly 200–300 µg/mL purified against about 1000 µg/mL crude lysate. Together these results show that the host, vector, and SUMO/His fusion design can produce soluble, purifiable protein, which supports the BL21 system as a suitable host. The parameters of our in vitro work were that we could not demonstrate that SulFlux or the F147S variants reliably fold correctly or sulfonate LCA, supporting only expression and purification, but no definitive catalytic activity.
